subject: MarketLytics DPA: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessor
messages:
From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@marketlytics.io>
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marketlytics-legal@marketlytics.io
Date: 2028-10-18T09:15:00Z
Subject: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and have a few redline asks before we can move to procurement sign-off for the November pilot: 

1) Retention of debug/telemetry snapshots: we need an explicit clause allowing MarketLytics to retain raw debug snapshots (error traces, request/response payloads) for up to 30 days to support debugging and regulatory audits.
2) Subprocessor allowance: we need MarketLytics-Insights (analytics partner) listed as an allowed subprocessor for telemetry/analytics with permission to access masked telemetry.
3) KMS integration: we plan to use our key management for logs exported to our environment; we need a brief carve-out to allow cross-account S3/KMS connection for exported telemetry.
4) No-training carveout: we want the option to request model performance analytics; we prefer that Redwood permit derivative telemetry to be used for product analytics (not model training).

I've attached our redline (MarketLytics_DPA_redline_20281018.pdf). Can you confirm whether these items are acceptable or if Redwood needs counter-language?

Procurement would like to close the DPA by Oct 31 to keep the project timeline.

Best,
Rajesh
Head of Partnerships
MarketLytics

Attachments: MarketLytics_DPA_redline_20281018.pdf

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2028-10-18T10:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Looping legal and product/security in — see MarketLytics' redline attached. Short summary of asks: 30-day raw debug snapshot retention, allow MarketLytics-Insights as analytics subproc, cross-account KMS/S3 export, ability to use telemetry for analytics (they say not training, but language is fuzzy). Procurement wants this done by 10/31 for the Nov pilot.

Questions for the thread:
- Legal: can we limit retention and require pseudonymization/auditing? Any auto-approval path for a named analytics vendor?
- Product/Security: technical risk of storing raw snapshots for 30 days + cross-account KMS — does this require feature work (engine, storage, or infra)?
- Sales/CS (Marcus/Priyom): timeline pressure and commercial concessions — what's our appetite to accept limited retention or insist on customer-managed storage?

Attaching the vendor redline here. I propose a quick sync if we can't converge by EOD.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MarketLytics_DPA_redline_20281018.pdf

From: olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-10-18T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Thanks Naomi — reviewed the attached redline. Top-line legal concerns: 

- The redline's "retain raw content" language is overly broad and would permit retention of unredacted PII in some telemetry fields. We should counter with explicit limits (session-level logs only) and mandatory masking/pseudonymization for any user identifiers.
- The subprocessor clause adds an open-ended allowances list and lacks evidence requirements. If we allow MarketLytics-Insights, we should require: SOC 2 Type II, a vendor security questionnaire, and contractual confirmation they will not use telemetry for model training.
- KMS cross-account language: acceptable only if encryption keys for exported logs are customer-controlled and we document the specific integration method. We should not permit Redwood-managed keys to be handed to third parties.

Suggested redline (short): "Redwood may export telemetry snapshots to Customer-managed storage for up to 30 days for debugging/audit purposes; exports must be to Customer-controlled accounts/buckets; any exported content must be pseudonymized unless expressly authorized in writing. MarketLytics-Insights may be designated as an analytics subprocessor only upon submission of SOC 2 report and completion of Redwood's vendor security review; no telemetry will be used to retrain Redwood models without prior written consent."

If Product/Security confirm this is technically acceptable, Legal can prepare a clean counter and send a DocuSign-ready amendment. Timeline: need confirmation by COB tomorrow to meet vendor's 10/31 goal.

-Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-10-18T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Quick technical notes from Product/Security: 

- Raw debug snapshots: storing full request/response payloads for 30 days is non-trivial. It increases storage, affects cache eviction policies, and carries risk of sensitive fields being captured. We can support this only if: (a) exports go to a customer-managed bucket (BYO-S3) OR (b) we implement an explicit feature flag that masks sensitive fields before persistence. Option (a) has lower product dev work but requires engineering involvement for the export integration (IAM/KMS alignment). Option (b) requires ~3 sprints of work to build masking and QA.
- Cross-account KMS: we can support cross-account exports but it requires an infra ticket and testing; latency is negligible but security review needed.
- Analytics subproc: limiting to MarketLytics-Insights OK if they pass our vendor security assessment and agree in writing not to use the telemetry for model training.

Impact to roadmap: if we go with Redwood-hosted retention plus masking, expect a feature window into Q1 2029. If the customer accepts BYO-S3 export (with our minimal engineering integration), we can target Nov pilot but need an engineering owner assigned this week.

CC: engineering should weigh in on cost estimate (I'll put a note in Jira).

-Soojin Lee
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-10-18T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Understand the constraints. MarketLytics is pushing hard on timelines — they need debug capabilities for their regulator demo in mid-Nov. Commercially I think we have a path: offer the BYO-S3 export approach with a limited 30-day retention and require MarketLytics to cover incremental storage and export costs (we'll provide estimate). In exchange, request: (1) signed attestation that MarketLytics-Insights will not train on telemetry; (2) SOC 2 evidence; (3) acceptance of our audit rights.

If Legal + Product are okay with the BYO-S3 + attestation approach, I can push procurement to accept the counter and include a commercial offset for the added operational work. Procurement will also want a line item to pay for the one-time integration/engineering effort.

-Marcus
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh@marketlytics.io>, procurement@marketlytics.io
Cc: olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com, soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, priyom_das@redwoodinference.com
Bcc: 
Date: 2028-10-18T16:00:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA amendment request: telemetry snapshots & analytics subprocessors

Rajesh — thank you for the redline and the clear timeline. We discussed internally and can propose the following compromise to enable your November pilot while minimizing production and compliance risk: 

1) Debug snapshots: Redwood will support export of debug/telemetry snapshots to a Customer-managed bucket (BYO-S3) for up to 30 days. Exports must be to a MarketLytics-owned account/bucket and use customer-managed KMS keys. Redwood will not persist full raw snapshots in Redwood-managed long-term storage.
2) Subprocessor: MarketLytics-Insights may be designated as an analytics subprocessor only after submission of a SOC 2 Type II report and completion of Redwood's vendor security questionnaire. The subprocessor will sign a binding attestation that telemetry will not be used to retrain Redwood models; any use for analytics (aggregate metrics) is permitted.
3) No-training / data use: add explicit clause — "Telemetry exported under this amendment shall not be used by Customer or Customer-designated subprocessors to retrain, fine-tune, or otherwise adapt Redwood Inference models without prior written consent."
4) Commercials / timeline: Redwood can deliver the BYO-S3 export integration for the Nov pilot provided MarketLytics accepts a one-time integration fee and covers storage costs. Marcus will share a cost estimate; Engineering needs assignment by 10/20 to meet timeline.

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the three bullets above and provide SOC 2 evidence for MarketLytics-Insights. If you agree, Legal will send a DocuSign amendment reflecting these points. Our target to close is 10/31.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
